CORAM: JUSTICE V. NARASINGH Date of hearing : 06.08.2025 Date of Judgment : 06.08.2025 V.
Narasingh, J. Heard learned counsel for the Appellant- Insurance Company and learned counsel for the Respondents-Claimants.
2.

The Appellant-Insurance Company has filed this appeal challenging the impugned judgment dated 22.05.2010 passed by the learned 1st M.A.C.T, Keonjhar in M.A.C No.313 of 2001 awarding compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of the application till the date of payment.
The Claimants have also filed cross-objection for enhancement of compensation amount.

3. The brief facts of the Claimants are that on 28.2.1999 while the deceased Gouri Mahanta along with other labourers were proceeding in the offending vehicle bearing registration number BHO-8707 from Kaliapani side towards Tamkia, the truck capsized on the road and the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died.

Alleging that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the Claimants filed claim case before the learned Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Opposite Party No.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle was set ex parte.
Appellant- Insurance Company appeared and filed its written statement denying the assertions made in the claim petition.

On the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed:
"1. Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ?
2. If so to what extent and from whom ?"
In order to substantiate the claim, Claimant- Petitioner No.1 examined himself as P.W.1 and one independent witness examined as P.W.2 and documents were exhibited on behalf of the Claimants and marked as Exts.1 to 5.
Neither oral nor documentary evidence has been adduced on behalf of the Insurance Company.

Considering the evidence on record, learned Tribunal directed for payment of compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- along with 7 % interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of payment.
5. Learned counsel for the Appellant-Insurance Company submits that on the alleged date of accident the vehicle was not validly insured with the Appellant- Insurance.
Hence, learned Tribunal erred in law in holding that the Appellant-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount.
He further submits that since the deceased was travelling in a goods vehicle, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the same.
Hence, the impugned order is liable to set aside.
6. Such submission is opposed by the learned counsel for the Claimants.

7. On a conspectus of the evidence on record and keeping in view the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sunita and others vrs. United India Insurance Company Ltd. and others1, this Court is of the considered view that the learned Tribunal after assessing the evidence on record has awarded just compensation.

entities.text: Sunita and others vrs. United India Insurance Company Ltd. and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.
It shall be open for the Insurance Company to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
8. Accordingly, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company and cross-objection filed by the Claimants stand dismissed.

9. Within six weeks of production of proof regarding deposit of the modified amount before the Tribunal, the statutory deposit along with accrued interest be refunded to the Appellant on proper application.
